messages:
maria: Heads-up — thinking through client-side hooks for A/B rollouts. Proposal: SDK exposes a deterministic assignment and injects an `x-redwood-variant` header on requests. Want the SDK to be able to operate offline and be sticky. Thoughts?

aj: +1 for deterministic local assignment for latency. But we can’t fully trust client headers for enforcement/metrics. Need a server-signed assignment or validation to avoid spoofing.

devon: For offline sticky: hash(user_id || salt) % 100 -> bucket. SDK can store assigned variant locally. When online, fetch authoritative assignment from /assign and reconcile.

kyle: Quick example for SDK -> server header (JS):
```js
const trace = uuidv4();
fetch('/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'x-redwood-variant': 'v2b',
    'x-redwood-trace': trace,
    'x-redwood-opt-in': 'true'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
});
```
Use `x-redwood-trace` for console linking.

sarah: We should support opt-in routing for privacy/regulatory reasons. Default should be opt-out (`x-redwood-opt-in: false`). Also, add `x-redwood-source: client` so telemetry can separate client- vs server-decided traffic.

olivia: Console requirements: per-variant dashboards (latency, cost, quality), and the ability to roll back or cut traffic by variant. Also need per-variant quota accounting so a sudden A/B spike doesn't blow committed spend.

aj: Guards: server-side kill-switch and max-traffic caps. Don’t accept raw `x-redwood-variant` headers unless they include a server signature (HMAC). Pattern: `x-redwood-variant: v2b; sig=abcd1234`. Server verifies sig before honoring for routing / billing.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout v2 -> v2b started at 10% across us-west/us-east at 11:03. Monitoring hooks active. :rocket:

maria: Sounds good. Proposed flow: SDK calls `/assign` once per install/session -> server returns `variant=v2b` + `sig`. SDK stores and attaches header `x-redwood-variant: v2b; sig=...`. If offline, fall back to deterministic hash. Reconcile server vs local on next online call.

devon: For hash-based fallback use `sha256(user_id + rollout_salt)` and map to buckets. Keep salt versioned so we can change assignment behavior without breaking stickiness permanently.

kyle: Mobile edge-case: when app initialized in airplane mode, use hash fallback but mark requests with `x-redwood-assignment: local-fallback`. Console can filter these.

sarah: Also add `x-redwood-optin-source` if user consent toggles routing. We must record consent TTL to avoid assigning users into experiments after they opt-out.

aj: Telemetry side: mark each event with `variant`, `variant_source` (server/client/local-fallback), and `trace_id`. Then rollup views show per-variant error rates. Also add quick alert: if variant error-rate > baseline + X within Y minutes -> auto-rollback.

maria: Security note — do not send PII in headers. Any identifier used by SDK for hashing should be a non-PII stable id (device id or hashed user id).

olivia: UX for rollouts console: show live % split, active guard conditions (error-threshold, latency-threshold), and ability to toggle accepting client-supplied variants (dev/test mode).

maria: I'll draft an RFC for: header formats (variant + sig + trace + source + opt-in), signature scheme, SDK offline fallback, and console telemetry labels. cc @aj @devon for validation and @olivia for console telemetry requirements.

kyle: tiny nit — use `x-redwood-variant: v2b;sig=...` (no spaces) to avoid parsing variability. Also include `x-redwood-variant-version` header if we need to rotate signing keys.

maria: Great. I'll put a first pass tonight. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
